why: I checked all four expect lines and their proofs. Each one can be checked at the PR head with local commands and a file read, and none needs a release, deploy or published page. Line 1 (run): a temp file plus `node src/app.js`, then checks on the exit code, the empty stdout and an exact grep on stderr (`bad config:`, the path, /line 3,? column 3|:3:3/). Line 2 (run): a one-line node import that prints OK or not, so there is one answer. Line 3 (run): a valid file must give 'listening on 9000' and exit 0. Line 4 is marked run but also asks the verifier to read test/config.test.js for a test asserting the path is in the message, then run `npm test` and look for '# fail 0'. All of these exist in the head checkout. The Node-version point about line/column is covered by the regex and the assumptions, so each check still has one answer.
